draft.title: The army and Rome's expansion
card: Rome began as a small city on the River Tiber, in central Italy. Over several centuries it came to control lands all around the Mediterranean Sea.
the main unit of the Roman army, made up of several thousand soldiers. Legions drilled often and fought in organised groups, so they were well trained and disciplined.
Rome fought Carthage, a powerful city in North Africa, in three wars called the Punic Wars. Rome won, and Carthage lost its power.
Victories brought Rome new land, wealth and people to rule. Its trained legions were one reason Rome could win and hold so much territory.
draft.remember: Well-trained legions helped a city on the Tiber grow into a Mediterranean power.

a.q: Why did Roman legions help Rome win its wars?
opts: They were trained and fought in organised groups
They were made up of sailors from Carthage
They were paid by the Senate to avoid fighting
They were chosen only from the richest families
a.why: Legions drilled often and fought in disciplined groups, which gave Rome an advantage in battle. Wealth of the soldiers is not mentioned as a reason, so the option about the richest families is wrong.
a.clue: Think about how legions practised and fought.

b.q: Rome fought three Punic Wars. Who was its opponent, and what was the result?
opts: Carthage, which lost its power to Rome
Carthage, which took over the city of Rome
Egypt, which became a Roman ally at once
Egypt, which lost its power to Rome
b.why: The Punic Wars were fought against Carthage in North Africa, and Rome won. Egypt is tempting because it was an ancient power, but it was not Rome's opponent in these wars.
b.clue: Carthage was a city in North Africa.

a.best: They were trained and fought in organised groups

b.best: Carthage, which lost its power to Rome

problems.detail: The clue 'Carthage was a city in North Africa' names the opponent. That rules out both Egypt options without the student knowing the idea and leaves a two-way choice. Use a clue that points to the card without naming the answer, such as 'Think about the powerful city across the sea in North Africa' or 'Think about which side won.'

The why says the 'richest families' option is wrong because wealth 'is not mentioned' on the card. That is weak reasoning. The option is wrong because legions were not drawn only from the richest families, and the card gives training and discipline as the reason they won.
